'''TP,''' formerly '''Teleperformance''', is a French [[multinational company|multinational]] [[business process outsourcing]] company founded in 1978 with headquarters in [[France]]. It provides services for debt collection, telemarketing, customer relationship management, [[content moderation]], and communication.<ref>{{cite web |title=Teleperformance |url=https://www.forbes.com/companies/teleperformance/ |website=Forbes}}</ref>

==History==

Daniel Julien created Teleperformance in June 1978, in [[Paris]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=La France championne du monde |date=29 March 2012 |url=https://www.lexpress.fr/economie/emploi/service-client-la-france-championne-du-monde_1098999.html}}</ref> In 1986, TP established international subsidiaries in [[Belgium]] and [[Italy]]. Two years later, TP expanded into [[Spain]], [[Germany]], [[Sweden]] and the [[United Kingdom]].{{fact|date=July 2026}}

Rochefortaise Communication merged with Teleperformance International in 1999 to form S.R. ance. This company became Teleperformance in 2006,<ref>{{Cite web |title=An Interview with Daniel Julien, Chief Executive Officer, Teleperformance Group Inc. |url=https://www.leadersmag.com/issues/2017.4_Oct/ROB/LEADERS-Daniel-Julien-Teleperformance-Group.html}}</ref> and shortened its name to TP in 2025.{{fact|date=July 2026}}

In 1992, TP USA was established, and Asia-Pacific contact centers were set up in the Philippines and Singapore in 1996. The Group expanded in Europe through numerous acquisitions and subsidiaries in Switzerland, Norway, Denmark, Greece, Spain, the Netherlands and Finland.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SR Teleperformance S.A |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/books/politics-and-business-magazines/sr-teleperformance-sa}}</ref> From 1998 through 2002, the TP network expanded into Argentina,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Company Overview of Teleperformance Argentina SA | website=[[Bloomberg News]] |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/Research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapid=39928788}}</ref> Brazil<ref>{{Cite web |title=Teleperformance abre nova unidade no Nordeste e irá gerar mais de 3.000 empregos |url=https://www.terra.com.br/noticias/teleperformance-abre-nova-unidade-no-nordeste-e-ira-gerar-mais-de-3000-empregos,b3ebb82b9a19ed10534000128b30b335is9kc5lx.html}}</ref> and Mexico.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Teleperformance Opens 17th Center in Mexico, with $6 Million Puebla Investment |date=18 June 2014 |url=https://nearshoreamericas.com/teleperformance-invests-6-million-call-center-puebla/}}</ref>

TP USA purchased [[AOL]]'s 400-employee call center in Ogden, Utah, in 2006.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Buffardi|first1=Michelle|title=Teleperformance USA Buys AOL Call Center |url=http://www.eetimes.com/document.asp?doc_id=1198225 |publisher=EE Times|access-date=4 September 2016|date=23 October 2006}}</ref>

In 2007, TP acquired a 100% interest in Twenty4help, a European technical support company, and AllianceOne, a US-based [[accounts receivable]] management company.<ref>{{cite web|title=French Call Center Giant Acquires Debt Collector AllianceOne|url=http://www.insidearm.com/daily/debt-collection-news/debt-collection/french-call-center-giant-acquires-debt-collector-allianceone/|publisher=Inside Arm|access-date=5 September 2016|date=1 August 2007|archive-date=20 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820021256/http://www.insidearm.com/daily/debt-collection-news/debt-collection/french-call-center-giant-acquires-debt-collector-allianceone/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2008, the group's operations and strategy were centralized under the responsibility of Daniel Julien and Jacques Berrebi. The same year, TP acquired The Answer Group.<ref>{{cite web|title=TELEPERFORMANCE ACQUIRES THE ANSWER GROUP|url=https://www.chiefmarketer.com/teleperformance-acquires-the-answer-group/|publisher=Chief Marketer|access-date=5 September 2016|date=24 December 2008}}</ref>

In 2010, TP acquired Scottish outsourcing call center beCogent for £35 million.<ref>{{Cite news|title=BeCogent call centre firm sold to Teleperformance|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-11007373|publisher=BBC|access-date=31 August 2016|date=18 August 2010}}</ref> It ceased operations in December 2021 mainly due to the impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and [[remote work]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/local-news/teleperformance-close-airdrie-contact-centre-23793142 | title=Teleperformance to close Airdrie contact centre base | date=25 March 2021 }}</ref> By 2013 TP had six contact centers in Tunisia.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Aizicovici | first1=Francine |title=Teleperformance et ses pratiques sociales "à l'épreuve" pour neuf mois | url=http://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2013/04/04/teleperformance-et-ses-pratiques-sociales-a-l-epreuve-pour-neuf-mois_3153415_3234.html?xtmc=teleperformance_et_ses_pratiques_sociales_a_l_epreuve_pour_neuf_mois&xtcr=1 |newspaper=Le Monde.fr |access-date=7 September 2016|date=4 April 2013}}</ref> In 2013, TP acquired full control of TLS Contact.<ref>{{cite web | title=TELEPERFORMANCE ACQUIERT 100% DE SA FILIALE TLSCONTACT | url=http://www.capital.fr/bourse/actualites/teleperformance-acquiert-100-de-sa-filiale-tlscontact-807130|publisher=Capital|access-date=7 September 2016 | date=29 January 2013|archive-date=16 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916120141/http://www.capital.fr/bourse/actualites/teleperformance-acquiert-100-de-sa-filiale-tlscontact-807130}}</ref> In 2014, TP acquired Aegis USA Inc., an outsourcing and technology company in the United States, the Philippines and Costa Rica.<ref name="610millions" />

In August 2016, TP purchased California-based LanguageLine Solutions LLC for $1.52 billion from a private equity firm Abry Partners.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ricadela |first1=Aaron |title=Teleperformance of France Buying LanguageLine for $1.52 Billion |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-08-22/teleperformance-of-france-buying-languageline-for-1-52-billion | work=[[Bloomberg News]] |access-date=13 September 2016 |date=22 August 2016}}</ref>

TP secured multiple [[United Kingdom government]] and [[NHS]] contracts to operate support services for the public during the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-16 |title=Contact centre firm Teleperformance reports significant growth through pandemic |url=https://www.irishnews.com/business/2022/06/16/news/contact-centre-firm-teleperformance-reports-significant-growth-through-pandemic-2744367/ |access-date=2024-04-08 |website=The Irish News |language=en}}</ref> In 2020, TP launched TP Cloud Campus in Portugal, with mobile cloud-enabled workstations for virtual onboarding, training, and employee meetings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Freire |first=Mafalda |date=2020-09-03 |title=Teleperformance lança novo modelo de negócio de trabalho remoto em equipa |url=https://business-it.pt/2020/09/03/teleperformance-lanca-novo-modelo-de-negocio-de-trabalho-remoto-em-equipa/ |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=Business-IT |language=pt-PT}}</ref> There are currently cloud campus hubs in the [[Philippines]] and [[Mexico]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-05-06 |title=Teleperformance conecta a México con las marcas más grandes del mundo a través del nearshoring |url=https://forbes.com.mx/teleperformance-conecta-a-mexico-con-las-marcas-mas-grandes-del-mundo-a-traves-del-nearshoring/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=Forbes México |language=es}}</ref>

In January 2024, TP completed the acquisition of [[Majorel]], acquiring 99% of the company's shares from [[Bertelsmann]] and Moroccan real estate company Saham,<ref name=Ammachchi>{{Cite web |last=Ammachchi |first=Narayan |date=2024-01-02 |title=Finally, Teleperformance Becomes Full Owner of Majorel - Nearshore Americas |url=https://nearshoreamericas.com/finally-teleperformance-becomes-full-owner-of-majorel/ |access-date=2024-07-15 |language=en}}</ref> in exchange for 3 billion euros and a 4% stake in TP.<ref name=Ammachchi/> This led to the launch of TP's digital consulting arm, TP Infinity, the same month.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-26 |title=Teleperformance Launches TP Infinity |url=https://www.destinationcrm.com/Articles/CRM-News/CRM-Across-the-Wire/Teleperformance-Launches-TP-Infinity-162355.aspx |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=CRM Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

TP announced a partnership with Sanas, a provider of software that uses AI to adjust a speaker's accent in real-time, in February 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiggers |first=Kyle |date=2025-02-19 |title=Sanas taps AI to change call center workers' accents in real time |url=https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/19/sanas-taps-ai-to-change-call-center-workers-accents-in-real-time/ |access-date=2025-05-12 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref> TP also made an equity investment of approximately $13 million in Sanas.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ziptone |date=2025-02-20 |title=Teleperformance acquires stake in Sanas |url=https://www.ziptone.nl/en/nieuws/teleperformance-neemt-belang-in-sanas/ |access-date=2025-05-12 |website=Ziptone - 100% klantcontact |language=en}}</ref>

TP and [[Carnegie Mellon University]] announced a partnership in March 2025 to accelerate AI applied research.<ref>{{cite web |title=TP, Teleperformance, acquires Agents Only, a Canadian Onepilot, without convincing: 78.54 euros |url=https://en-contact.com/tp-teleperformance-acquires-agents-only-a-canadian-onepilot-without-convincing-7854-euros |website=En-contact |access-date=16 July 2025 |language=fr}}</ref>

In June 2025, TP purchased Vancouver-based AI crowdsourcing platform Agents Only.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Craig |date=2025-06-23 |title=Teleperformance acquires Agents Only |url=https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/teleperformance-acquires-agents-only |access-date=2025-07-25 |website=Staffing Industry Analysts (SIA) |language=en}}</ref> The company also launched TP.ai, an AI orchestration platform.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Rhodes |first1=Dimitri |last2=Lhomedet |first2=Hugo |date=2025-06-18 |title=TP aims to hand back 1.5 billion euros to shareholders by 2028 |url=https://www.aol.com/news/tp-aims-hand-back-1-124832030.html |access-date=2025-07-25 |website=AOL |language=en}}</ref>

=== Governance ===
Jacques Berrebi ended all operational duties in January 2009 and returned in 2012, at the age of 70.<ref>{{cite web |title=TELEPERFORMANCE: Jacques Berrebi organizes his retirement |url=http://www.marketwired.com/press-release/teleperformance-jacques-berrebi-organizes-his-retirement-paris-rcf-795022.htm |publisher=Market Wired |access-date=5 September 2016 |date=30 November 2007 |archive-date=17 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917021122/http://www.marketwired.com/press-release/teleperformance-jacques-berrebi-organizes-his-retirement-paris-rcf-795022.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Co-founder Daniel Julien remained as chairman of the board, and Paulo César Salles Vasques was announced as the new chief executive officer of the group.<ref name="610millions">{{cite web |last1=Robert |first1=Martine |title=Teleperformance mise 610 millions sur les Etats-Unis |url=http://www.lesechos.fr/10/07/2014/LesEchos/21726-062-ECH_teleperformance-mise-610-millions-sur-les-etats-unis.htm |publisher=Les Echos |access-date=7 September 2016|date=10 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Teleperformance vise une nouvelle année de croissance en 2014|url=http://investir.lesechos.fr/actions/actualites/teleperformance-vise-une-nouvelle-annee-de-croissance-en-2014-953925.php|publisher=Les Echos|access-date=7 September 2016|date=7 September 2016}}</ref>

Following Vasques' resignation in October 2017, Julien was appointed as group chief executive officer by the board of directors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.teleperformance.com/en-us/investor-relations/corporate-governance-and-sri/governance-structure |title=GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE |date=13 October 2017}}</ref> In June 2023,  Bhupender Singh was appointed as TP Group Deputy Chief Executive Officer.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Teleperformance Appoints Bhupender Singh as Deputy Chief Executive Officer |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20230618763146/en/Teleperformance-Appoints-Bhupender-Singh-as-Deputy-Chief-Executive-Officer | publisher=[[Business Wire]] |date=2023-06-19}}</ref> In August 2024, Olivier Rigaudy, Agustin Grisanti and Scott Klein were appointed as deputy CEOs,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-30 |title=Teleperformance: departure of Bhupender Singh, recall of Majorel's old guard |url=https://experienceclient-thefrenchforum.org/teleperformance-departure-of-bhupender-singh-recall-of-majorels-old-guard/ |access-date=2024-10-21 |website=The French Forum |language=fr-FR}}</ref> and when Singh departed in October 2024, his role was assumed by Thomas Mackenbrock.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Quiret |first=Matthew |date=2024-08-24 |title=Teleperformance's new leaders watch for the AI bubble to burst |url=https://www.lesechos.fr/industrie-services/services-conseils/les-nouveaux-dirigeants-de-teleperformance-guettent-lexplosion-de-la-bulle-de-lia-2115720 |website=Les Echos |language=fr}}</ref>

In March 2026, founder and CEO Daniel Julien stepped down from his executive role and transitioned to the position of Strategic Advisor to the Chairman & CEO. Deputy CEO Thomas Mackenbrock and Deputy CEO of Finance Olivier Rigaudy also stepped down from their executive roles. Benoît Gabelle, currently Deputy CFO, was appointed interim Chief Financial Officer. Jorge Amar, a global expert in AI-native customer operations at scale, was appointed Group Chief Executive Officer.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=TP: 2025 Annual Results |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260226645110/en/TP-2025-Annual-Results |access-date=12 March 2026 |website=Business Wire}}</ref>

=== Corporate social responsibility ===
TP's Citizen of the World program helped relocate and build homes for the victims of the [[Typhoon Ketsana]] in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Teleperformance Receives the PEZA Outstanding Community Project of the Year Award. - Free Online Library |url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Teleperformance+Receives+the+PEZA+Outstanding+Community+Project+of...-a0328896163 |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=www.thefreelibrary.com}}</ref> Since 2006, Citizen of the World has made $60 million in donations to assist vulnerable populations in 50 countries.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date= |title=Teleperformance says it had assisted 60,000 children, including 10,000 from India, in 2022 |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/teleperformance-says-it-had-assisted-60000-children-including-10000-from-india-in-2022/article66440847.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230127160715/https://www.thehindu.com/business/teleperformance-says-it-had-assisted-60000-children-including-10000-from-india-in-2022/article66440847.ece |url-status=live |archive-date=27 January 2023 |access-date=2025-01-22 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |url-access=limited|issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-09 |title=Teleperformance donates to Southern Philippines Medical Center frontliners |url=https://www.manilatimes.net/2021/07/09/public-square/teleperformance-donates-to-southern-philippines-medical-center-frontliners/1806306 |access-date=2025-01-22 |website=The Manila Times |language=en}}</ref>

TP partnered with One Tree Planted in 2022, funding the plantation of 500,000 trees across Europe, Asia, and the Americas.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Welch |first=Dylan |date=2022-12-06 |title=Teleperformance propels reforestation with One Tree Planted |url=https://green.org/2022/12/06/teleperformance-propels-reforestation-with-one-tree-planted/ |access-date=2024-11-12 |website=Green.org |language=en-US}}</ref> Also in 2022, TP entered a partnership with the [[Negros Occidental]] provincial government, to give priority to Negros Occidental Language Information Technology Center graduates in job applications.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Digicast Negros |date=2022-07-27 |title=NOLITC signs partnership with Teleperformance |url=https://digicastnegros.com/nolitc-signs-partnership-with-teleperformance/ |access-date=2025-01-22 |website=Digicast Negros |language=en-US}}</ref>

Since 2022, TP has partnered with UNICEF to help protect and advance children’s rights, with a focus on quality education in areas most in need, like Brazil, Ghana, and the Philippines. TP also supports UNICEF’s Global Humanitarian Thematic Fund, contributing to emergency responses in countries and regions including Sudan, Ukraine, Syria, Türkiye, Nigeria, and Latin America and the Caribbean.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first= UNICEF |date=2022-07-27 |title=TP for UNICEF |url=https://www.unicef.org/partnerships/tp |access-date=202-09-15 |website=UNICEF |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Controversies ==
In 2008 a [[class action]] lawsuit was filed against Salt Lake City-based Teleperformance USA seeking [[Wage theft|unpaid wages]] for employees, alleging a violation of the [[Fair Labor Standards Act]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=Chris |date=10 September 2008 |title=Only on 12: Teleperformance facing class action lawsuit |url=http://www.wrdw.com/home/headlines/28203894.html |access-date=31 August 2016 |publisher=WRDW12 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Dogooder-810978 |date=11 January 2009 |title=Wage and Hour Class Action Lawsuit Against Teleperformance |url=http://dogooder2.newsvine.com/_news/2009/01/12/2300917-wage-and-hour-class-action-lawsuit-against-teleperformance |access-date=31 August 2016 |publisher=Newsvine}}</ref> On 19 May 2010, a settlement was reached for approximately $2 million to be paid to 15,862 workers in 10 US states.<ref>{{cite web |date=19 May 2010 |title=Salt Lake City-based Teleperformance USA pays almost $2 million in back overtime wages following US Department of Labor investigation |url=https://www.dol.gov/opa/media/press/whd/whd20100633.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100527110008/http://www.dol.gov/opa/media/press/whd/WHD20100633.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 May 2010 |access-date=31 August 2016 |publisher=US Dept of Labor}}</ref> Instead of an out of court settlement, TP lost a similar case in the Netherlands Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal in The Hague.<ref>{{cite web |last1=ANP |title=Supreme Court rules that obliged early arrival for work counts as paid hours|url=https://nltimes.nl/2024/09/13/supreme-court-rules-obliged-early-arrival-work-counts-paid-hours |website=NL Times | date=2024-09-13}}</ref>

A group of labor unions filed a complaint documenting unsafe working conditions, monitoring, surveillance, union busting and retaliation against employees in ten countries in April 2020.  Due to [[COVID-19]] restrictions, workers in the [[Philippines]], including those supporting [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]]'s [[Ring (company)|Ring camera]] contract, had to sleep at their work spaces and were unable to meet [[social distancing]] requirements. The ''[[Financial Times]]'' was able to verify this, including in a [[Cebu City]] office.<ref name="subhuman" /> After the working conditions were made public, the company promised to make improvements, but [[NBC News]] reported after six months the company was providing intermittent shuttle service, not properly sanitizing working spaces, and sending workers home without pay if they were quarantined.<ref name="subhuman">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Dave |date=1 April 2020 |title=Amazon contractors enduring 'subhuman' conditions in Philippines {{!}} Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/8b7bc787-4f33-4909-85f0-8df36d165b69 |access-date=8 August 2023 |work=ft.com}}</ref><ref name="Highrisk">{{Cite web |last1=Solon |first1=Olivia |last2=Glaser |first2=April |date=15 October 2020 |title=High risk, low pay, little choice at Amazon Ring call centre, fearful workers say |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/security/we-don-t-have-choice-amazon-ring-call-center-workers-n1243439 |access-date=8 August 2023 |work=NBC News}}</ref>

In 2021, TP employees who work from home were sent contract addendums that would allow monitoring by AI-powered cameras to ensure compliance with security policies and to spot check for home-working infractions.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Peter |date=26 March 2021 |title=Call centre staff to be monitored via webcam for home-working 'infractions' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/mar/26/teleperformance-call-centre-staff-monitored-via-webcam-home-working-infractions |access-date=8 August 2023 |work=the Guardian}}</ref><ref name="nn">{{Cite web |last=Solon |first=Olivia |date=8 August 2021 |title=Big Tech call center workers face pressure to accept home surveillance |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/big-tech-call-center-workers-face-pressure-accept-home-surveillance-n1276227 |access-date=8 August 2023 |work=NBC News}}</ref> As of August that year, the remote monitoring had been rolled out to India, Mexico, and the Philippines.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Peter |date=26 March 2021 |title='Missing from desk': AI webcam raises remote surveillance concerns |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/mar/26/missing-from-desk-ai-webcam-raises-remote-surveillance-concerns |access-date=8 August 2023 |work=the Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Lavelle |first1=Moira |title="For them you're not a human being": Meet the migrants answering phones for Big Tech |url=https://restofworld.org/2021/call-center-greece-teleperformance/ |website=restofworld|date=13 May 2021 }}</ref> UK employees were told remote scans would not be used for them,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Walker |first1=Peter |title=Call centre firm tells UK homeworkers they will not be watched with webcam |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/apr/21/call-centre-teleperformance-tells-homeworkers-they-will-not-be-watched-webcam |website=The Guardian|date=21 April 2021 }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> and [[Albania]] ruled out the use of webcams through their Data Protection Commission.<ref name="nn" /> An [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] spokesperson reported Apple "prohibits the use of video or photographic monitoring by our suppliers and have confirmed TP does not use video monitoring for any of their teams working with Apple."<ref name="nn" />

[[Uber]] reported that it requested the following [[Audit trail|audit logs]] for its workers: monitoring to verify that only a hired employee is accessing data; that outsourced staff were not recording screen data on another device; and that no unauthorized person was near the computer.<ref name="nn" /> An Amazon spokesperson reported Amazon did not request additional monitoring for at-home workers.<ref name="nn" />

In [[Colombia]], the union Utraclaro, affiliated to [[UNI Global Union]], has organized TP Colombia employees, including [[Content moderators|moderators]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=McIntyre |first=Niamh |date=19 April 2023 |title=Teleperformance signs 'historic agreement' allowing Colombian workers to unionise |work=[[The Bureau of Investigative Journalism]] |url=https://www.thebureauinvestigates.com/stories/2023-04-19/teleperformance-signs-historic-agreement-allowing-colombian-workers-to-unionise |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 2021, after the union submitted its demands for the company to protect [[freedom of association]], TP filed a lawsuit against the union in a [[labor court]], alleging Ultraclaro did not follow proper processes when ratifying its [[Collective bargaining|bargaining demands]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=McIntyre |first1=Niamh |last2=Bradbury |first2=Rosie |last3=Perrigo |first3=Billy |date=20 October 2022 |title=Behind TikTok's boom: A legion of traumatised, $10-a-day content moderators |work=[[The Bureau of Investigative Journalism]] |url=https://www.thebureauinvestigates.com/stories/2022-10-20/behind-tiktoks-boom-a-legion-of-traumatised-10-a-day-content-moderators |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> In November 2022, the [[Ministry of Labour (Colombia)|Ministry of Labour]] launched an investigation into the company.<ref name=Traumatic>{{Cite magazine |last=Perrigo |first=Billy |date=10 November 2022 |title=TikTok's Subcontractor in Colombia Under Investigation for Traumatic Work |url=https://time.com/6231625/tiktok-teleperformance-colombia-investigation/ |magazine=[[TIME]] |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> After the announcement of the investigation, shares in the company dropped by 34%.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-10 |title=France's Teleperformance to buy back shares after sell-off on probe news |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/frances-teleperformance-launch-share-buyback-2022-11-10/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> In December 2022, the subsidiary received independent certification from [[Bureau Veritas]] on the "use and inclusion of the international standard [[ISO 26000]] in the field of social responsibility within its operations in Colombia."<ref name=":0">{{cite news|title=TELEPERFORMANCE : A REÇU UNE CERTIFICATION DE BUREAU VERITAS|url=https://www.tradingsat.com/teleperformance-FR0000051807/actualites/teleperformance-teleperformance-a-recu-une-certification-de-bureau-veritas-1047443.html|date=7 December 2022|website=www.tradingsat.com}}</ref>

In April and May 2023, the company signed a [[Global Framework Agreement|global framework agreement]] enabling workers in Colombia, [[Romania]] and [[Poland]] to unionize.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Teleperformance signs 'historic agreement' allowing Colombian workers… |url=https://www.thebureauinvestigates.com/stories/2023-04-19/teleperformance-signs-historic-agreement-allowing-colombian-workers-to-unionise/ |access-date=2024-08-21 |website=TBIJ |language=en}}</ref> The Ministry of Labor later closed their investigation into TP, without any findings against the company.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cantu |first=Cesar |date=2024-07-23 |title=Why is Colombia's Labor Ministry Cracking Down on Call Centers? - Nearshore Americas |url=https://nearshoreamericas.com/why-is-colombias-labor-ministry-cracking-down-on-call-centers/ |access-date=2024-08-21 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=infotech |date=2023-07-29 |title=BPO major Teleperformance reports €3.96 bn revenue in first-half |url=https://infotechlead.com/bpo/bpo-major-teleperformance-reports-e3-96-bn-revenue-in-first-half-79685#:~:text=In%20April%20and%20May%202023,any%20findings%20against%20the%20company |access-date=2024-08-21 |website=InfotechLead |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-22 |title=City of Warren Gen. Emps' Sys. v. Teleperformance SE, 23-24580-CIV-ALTONAGA/Reid {{!}} Casetext Search + Citator |url=https://casetext.com/case/city-of-warren-gen-emps-sys-v-teleperformance-se |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240821115903/https://casetext.com/case/city-of-warren-gen-emps-sys-v-teleperformance-se |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 August 2024 |access-date=2024-08-21 |website=casetext.com}}</ref>

In February 2024, TP received a certificate for diversity and inclusion management in Colombia from [[AENOR]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zonebourse |date=2024-02-22 |title=Teleperformance : certifié diversité et inclusion en Colombie - Zonebourse |url=https://www.zonebourse.com/cours/action/TELEPERFORMANCE-SE-4709/actualite/Teleperformance-certifie-diversite-et-inclusion-en-Colombie-46008196/ |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=www.zonebourse.com |language=fr}}</ref>

===Content moderation===
{{See also|Content moderation and working conditions}}
TP employs [[Content moderation|content moderators]] for platforms including [[TikTok]], with moderators in [[Tunisia]] and [[Colombia]], reviewing explicit content to remove it from the platform.<ref name="Moderators" /><ref name="Traumatic" /> Its "[[Trust and safety|Trust and Safety]]" branch and moderation program were launched in 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Levine |first=Alexandra S. |date=4 Aug 2022 |title=TikTok Moderators Are Being Trained Using Graphic Images Of Child Sexual Abuse |work=[[Forbes]] |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexandralevine/2022/08/04/tiktok-is-storing-uncensored-images-of-child-sexual-abuse-and-using-them-to-train-moderators/?sh=22a35dca5acb |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> After an investigation by ''[[Forbes]]'' reported the company retained explicit material, TP and TikTok were criticized by the [[United States Senate Committee on Commerce]] and by shareholders.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Levine |first=Alexandra S. |date=17 Nov 2022 |title=Top TikTok Moderator Exits 'Highly Egregious Part' Of Content Moderation Business Over Investor Outcry |work=[[Forbes ]]|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexandralevine/2022/11/17/top-tiktok-moderator-exits-highly-egregious-part-of-content-moderation-business-over-investor-outcry/?sh=48c789473743 |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> In November 2022, the company announced that it would exit "the highly egregious part of the trust and safety business." However, it reversed its decision in March 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Berthelot |first=Benoit |date=23 March 2023 |title=TikTok's Moderator Reverses Vow to Exit 'Egregious' Content |work=[[Bloomberg Law]] |url=https://news.bloomberglaw.com/privacy-and-data-security/tiktoks-moderator-reverses-pledge-to-exit-egregious-content |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="Moderators">{{Cite web |title=TikTok's Moderators Still Review Child Abuse Despite Vow to Exit |first1=Benoit |last1=Berthelot |first2=Henry |last2=Ren |work=Bloomberg.com |date=19 March 2023 |access-date=8 August 2023 |url= https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-03-20/tiktok-s-moderators-still-review-child-abuse-despite-vow-to-exit#xj4y7vzkg}}</ref> In 2025, the company is discovered to operate content moderation for Meta in the Ghanaian capital of Accra, which faced criticism for poor working conditions, low pay, and mental health affects on moderators.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meta's content moderators face worst conditions yet at secret Ghana… |url=https://www.thebureauinvestigates.com/stories/2025-04-27/suicide-attempts-sackings-and-a-vow-of-silence-metas-new-moderators-face-worst-conditions-yet |access-date=2025-05-04 |website=TBIJ |language=en}}</ref>

Following the announcement, [[UNI Global Union]] released a statement, stating "we believe that TP's decision to re-enter full-service content moderation is a positive step."<ref>{{Cite web |title=UNI's statement on Teleperformance continuing full-service content moderation |url=https://uniglobalunion.org/news/unis-statement-on-teleperformance-continuing-full-service-content-moderation/ |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=UNI Global Union |language=en-GB}}</ref>
